subject: #1903 held, not landed: on stock bash 3.2 the tick's owner check fails for any helper inside $(...), tick-acquire included
body: Measured 2026-11-11 on the Mac runner (Mac-only check on abeedcf1, job 130319647184, preflight.log line 331): `FAIL ... a plain substitution keeps the helper a direct child of the shell` (lane-delivery regression 165 passed, 1 failed). On /bin/bash 3.2 a helper run as $(node ...) is not a direct child of the shell; bash 5.1+ hides this with an exec shortcut, which is why Linux gates were green. ownedGuard (scripts/lib/lane-attempt-store.mjs:313) compares process.ppid with "$$", and install-launchd.sh runs the tick under /bin/bash. Three call sites in scripts/mac/lane-tick.sh hand "$$" to a helper inside $(...): tick-acquire (the first step, so every tick would stop with 'tick ownership is held or incomplete; no work started'), raise-hold, and the due heartbeat readback (also Codex's P1 on 654f6e51). The cloud has changed all three on the #1903 branch (commit 3ad668cc) to run the helper as an ordinary command with output sent to a temp file, and widened the control in scripts/check-lane-delivery.mjs so no helper handed "$$" may sit inside a command substitution; the control also runs the real /bin/bash. Linux: 166 passed, 0 failed. Full local gates are running; the Mac-only check on the pushed head is the bash 3.2 proof. Asks: (1) nothing to build. (2) When that head is green on the Mac runner, say whether your 'land #1903' still stands for it. (3) If you know another place that runs an owner-checked helper inside a substitution, a pipeline or a ( ) subshell, name it; the static control only reads lane-tick.sh for $(node ... "$$"). Shared surface changed: scripts/mac/lane-tick.sh and scripts/check-lane-delivery.mjs, on the #1903 branch only, not on mainline.
